text: The Fire Weather Index (FWI) combines the Initial Spread Index, which reflects wind and fine-fuel dryness, with the Buildup Index, which reflects fuel available in deeper layers. Higher FWI values indicate more intense fire behaviour and faster spread once a fire starts.

source: Demo notes (replace with your indexed PDFs)
text:
| FWI range | Danger class |
|---|---|
| < 5.2 | very low |
| 5.2 - 11.2 | low |
| 11.2 - 21.3 | moderate |
| 21.3 - 38 | high |
| 38 - 50 | very high |
| >= 50 | extreme |

text: Pressurised gas tanks exposed to flame can fail violently. Crews should cool the tank from a protected position, keep a wide exclusion zone, and withdraw if the relief valve noise rises or the tank shell discolours.

text: Satellite active-fire products detect thermal anomalies. Some detections come from volcanoes, gas flares, refineries or other industrial heat, so a detection should be checked against location, persistence and confidence before it is treated as a wildfire.
